prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Helpful changes: Reordering onboarding flow sequences, targeted functional hints (photo upload, path helper, sign-in security), select layouts (card carousel, single-click identity), key desktop flows (summon, visibility & control), and specific shortcut copy changes drove significant wins.
Harmful changes: Major structural redesigns (split personality), intrusive setup flows (desktop docking setup), spotlight path selector layouts, account persistence hints, and specific copy changes caused significant performance drops and early stops.
No clear effect: Wait, progress, and status indicators, background notifications, tutorial/showcase screens, and incentive badges consistently showed no clear effect.
Predictions too high: Large predicted gains (+8.0% and above) consistently overestimated actual performance, frequently resulting in smaller gains, no clear effect, or early test cutoffs.
Predictions too low: Major winning changes—especially shortcut copy, key desktop flows (visibility & control, summon flow), and story-first reordering—far exceeded low or negative predictions.

Changes:
0: [home, new_flow] Desktop Interactivity Companion Flow: Add an interactive desktop widget preview sub-flow on the waiting screen where users practice summoning and placing their pet while graphics compile. (why: Home waiting stage has a massive mean time of 2336s, and support logs show users are confused about how to display or control the pet on their desktop after onboarding.)
1: [sign_in, reorder] Post Companion Adoption Sign-In Sequence: Reorder the onboarding flow so user sign-in takes place after photo upload and adoption certificate creation, right before the waiting phase. (why: Moving account sign-in after pet customization builds ownership and intent, boosting overall funnel conversion from the low 32.9% baseline.)
2: [choose_path, new_screen] Companion Persona Preview Screen: Insert a new introductory screen before path selection featuring short animated previews of different pet companion behaviors. (why: The choose_path step has an extremely high mean duration of 514s, indicating decision paralysis when choosing companion behavior paths without context.)
3: [finish, copy] Desktop Hotkey Control Launch Copy: Update the home completion screen headline and body to explicitly explain desktop hotkeys for showing, hiding, and speaking to the pet. (why: Support emails show post-onboarding confusion regarding how to summon, control, or hide the pet once on the desktop.)
4: [choose_path, layout] Path Choice Carousel Layout: Switch the choose_path screen layout to a dynamic swipeable card carousel to highlight each path option clearly. (why: Choose path drop-off and high mean time (514s) show users need cleaner visual presentation to pick a path confidently.)
5: [sign_in, hint] Account Restore Identity Security Hint: Add a prominent security hint on the sign-in screen informing users that signing in restores existing pets and prevents profile loss. (why: 8 support emails (the single largest complaint theme) were about missing or reset pets after signing back in.)
6: [home, wait_info] Desktop Background Setup Context Info: Update waiting screen text to provide clear technical context on background desktop engine initialization and asset compilation. (why: High mean waiting duration (2336s) leads users to think the desktop companion app has stalled or failed.)
7: [adoption, copy] Adoption Certificate Action Confirmation Copy: Update adoption_certificate screen headline and primary button label to emphasize official companion binding. (why: Adoption is the funnel's lowest converting stage (64.2%), requiring clear, high-intent call-to-action copy.)

scores.note: Key desktop summoning and control flows are strong drivers of success, though interactive UI has high cost.
Reordering sequences to build intent before sign-in aligns with historical wins and tested sign_in reorder gains.
Showcase and preview screens show no clear effect in past tests and carry high build cost.
Shortcut copy changes addressing desktop pet controls are proven winners and low cost.
Card carousel layout changes are explicitly highlighted as successful layout improvements.
High support email volume points here, but account persistence hints are explicitly listed as harmful changes.
Wait, progress, and technical status context indicators consistently show no clear effect.
Adoption step has the funnel's biggest drop-off (35.8%), giving high impact potential despite mixed copy test results.
